label: rem:q-dilogarithm-pentagon-associator
title: The $q$-dilogarithm pentagon as the monoidal associator axiom
html:
The q-dilogarithm is not imported into the framework as a separate datum; it is the solution of a coherence condition the substrate category \mathbf{C} already carries. Because \mathbf{C} is monoidal, its associator \alpha_{X,Y,Z}\colon (X\otimes Y)\otimes Z \to X\otimes(Y\otimes Z) satisfies the Mac Lane pentagon coherence — the five reassociations of a fourfold tensor commute. Passing to the shuffle Hopf algebra \mathcal{H}_q of the braiding, that coherence descends to a functional equation on the level-2 shuffle primitive: the five reassociations collapse to the five-term relation

  \mathrm{Li}_2^q(y) + \mathrm{Li}_2^q(x) = \mathrm{Li}_2^q(xy) + \mathrm{Li}_2^q\!\left(\frac{x(1-y)}{1-xy}\right) + \mathrm{Li}_2^q\!\left(\frac{y(1-x)}{1-xy}\right).

By the definition of the q-dilogarithm there is exactly one level-2 primitive satisfying this relation, so the pentagon axiom names \mathrm{Li}_2^q rather than merely constraining it — the dilogarithm is the unique scalar shadow of the associator. In operator form this is the Faddeev–Kashaev identity: the quantum dilogarithm is the quantum associator (equivalently the 6j-symbol), and the operator pentagon

  \Phi(\mathsf P)\,\Phi(\mathsf Q) = \Phi(\mathsf Q)\,\Phi(\mathsf P+\mathsf Q)\,\Phi(\mathsf P)

on a Weyl pair \mathsf P\mathsf Q = \mathsf Q\mathsf P + 1 is the same coherence read as a fusion move.

The equivalence of the pentagon with the q-dilogarithm, proved below, is scalar: a potential on \mathcal{H}_q satisfies the five-term relation exactly when it is a q-dilogarithm datum. The reduction from the morphism-level Mac Lane pentagon on \alpha_{X,Y,Z} to that scalar equation is the classical shuffle--associator identification of Faddeev--Kashaev, and the analytic five-term relation at q \neq 1 remains conjectural. So the pentagon names \mathrm{Li}_2^q within the scalar layer, and the passage from the categorical axiom to that layer rests on the cited identification.

Two faces of the one associator. On the substrate branch (real q) the pentagon is realised by the compact dilogarithm \Phi_q / \mathrm{Li}_2^q — the bar-even face that drives mass and binding. Continued to the fibre branch |q|=1, where the compact product's zeros accumulate on the unit circle and it ceases to be well defined, the surviving realisation is Faddeev's non-compact modular double \Phi_b = \Phi_{1/b} (with q = e^{2\pi i b^2}) — the bar-odd face carrying the decay observable. Both solve the same pentagon; they are the two archimedean lenses of the identification of the \Phi_q machinery with the AJ-conjecture machinery in the stochastic-mechanics chapter (real versus root-of-unity saddle of the one \hat{A}_K), not two different objects.

The observable is a pairing, not a product. Where an archimedean number is finally extracted, the dilogarithm associator enters as an analytic operator paired against the algebraic Markov-trace state — a Hopf–Drinfeld pairing (equivalently a q-difference-module action), not a scalar multiplication: the continuous flow is contracted against the finite cyclotomic trace data. This "analytic paired with algebraic" structure fixes the shape of the observable. It does not, by itself, determine the analytic monodromy datum away from the roots of unity — that datum is genuinely resurgent and remains open.

Sources for the operator pentagon and the 6j reading. For complex b in the first quadrant, Faddeev, Kashaev and Volkov prove the five-term identity e_b(\mathsf P)\,e_b(\mathsf X) = e_b(\mathsf X)\,e_b(\mathsf P + \mathsf X)\,e_b(\mathsf P) for self-adjoint \mathsf P, \mathsf X with [\mathsf P, \mathsf X] = 1/(2\pi i), and obtain real b by continuity [faddeev-kashaev-volkov2000, \S6.1, eq. (20), and \S6.5]; with q = e^{i\pi b^2}, complex b in that quadrant gives |q| < 1, and the unitary case |q| = 1 is reached by continuity. Their commutator is normalised by 1/(2\pi i), where the display above uses \mathsf P\mathsf Q = \mathsf Q\mathsf P + 1, so the two agree after rescaling the pair. The identification of the elementary intertwiners attached to diagonal exchanges of ideal triangulations with the Kashaev 6j-symbols is recorded by Baseilhac and Benedetti, who attribute it to earlier work and derive the matrix dilogarithms of the quantum hyperbolic state sums from those 6j-symbols [baseilhac-benedetti-fibred, \S1]. A semiclassical anchor comes from Teschner and Vartanov: as b \to 0, the b-6j symbol of the modular double localises at the two roots u_\pm of dU/du = -2\pi i/u, where U(u,A) is an alternating sum of eight dilogarithms in A_k = e^{i\eta_k}, with exponent W_\pm(A)/(2\pi i b^2), W_\pm(A) = U(u_\pm, A) + \Delta(A) - \tfrac53\pi^2 \mp 2\pi^2\varphi, whose imaginary part is the hyperbolic tetrahedron volume formula they quote from Murakami and Yano [terashima-yamazaki2013, \S\S3.1--3.2, eqs. (3.1)--(3.4) and (3.10)--(3.11)]. Those tetrahedra are non-ideal, fixed by six free dihedral angles, so the anchor does not by itself give \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) or any ideal-triangulation volume; that would need the ideal limit of their eq.~(3.3).
